The probability formula itself (confirmed live against the compiled UReal#calculate, not read off source alone) is genuinely counter-intuitive: for two Gaussians with equal sigma, P(A<B) is exactly 0 whenever mean(A) > mean(B), not a small tail probability -- the crossing-point method this datatype library uses is not the naive independent-difference formula a reasonable first guess would assume. kk-modelvalidator.evidence: transform/ocl/DefaultExpressionVisitor.java visitLet() lines 234-258
kk-modelvalidator.notes: Handles both scalar and collection-valued let-bound variables (registers into collectionVariables when visitor.isSet()), and correctly threads variableClasses for object-typed lets so later attribute/navigation lookups on the let-variable resolve; correctly removes bindings after the in-expression.

unc-modelvalidator.evidence: ExpressionTranslator.visitLet() (line 1322) dispatches to objectAnyLet() (line 1374) for class-typed let variables, or the primitive scalar path for Integer/Boolean/Real/String (refusing every other type at the same site -- String added 2026-08-28, see notes: nothing about the native SMT-LIB let mechanism is type-specific, and String was already encoded as an Integer domain index, so the prior 3-type gate excluded a case the underlying machinery already handled). Primitive scalar lets: native SMT-LIB `let` bindings for both value and explicit definedness (LocalBinding, threaded through the whole visitor via localBindings so a let-bound variable stays resolvable inside nested forAll/exists/iterate bodies); verified against the real pinned Z3 5.1.0 binary and against ExpLet.eval()'s own undefined-propagation semantics (an undefined bound value makes the whole let undefined, not either branch). Object-typed lets: objectAnyLet() (1374) supports exactly `let x = T.allInstances()->any(pred) in body` as a finite disjunction over PolymorphicRange candidate slots, selecting the first matching slot in stable order; deliberately restricted to strict ordered-comparison bodies over the let-variable's own attributes (isStrictObjectLetBody, line 1436) since a non-strict body (e.g. equality against oclUndefined) would need a first-class undefined-object representation this encoder does not have. collectionSize() (1235) was extended to support size() over `X.allInstances()->select(pred)`, guarded so a select whose source is NOT allInstances still falls through to the original, pre-existing refusal message (a regression the managing session found and fixed: the extension had redirected that case to a different, select-specific message, breaking the pre-existing SizeTranslationTest.selectFilteredSourceFailsClosed). A narrow `div` (line 415, dispatched via the visitStdOp switch's new `case "div"` at line 277) supports exactly `Integer div (X.allInstances()->select(pred)->size())`: the divisor is a non-constant SMT term (a filtered population count), and SMT-LIB div with a non-numeral divisor is nonlinear arithmetic under this project's pinned QF_LIA logic -- confirmed directly against the real Z3 binary, the exact same restriction requireLinearProduct already documents for `*`. The fix is a case-split over the population's own Java-side candidate-slot count (a compile-time-known bound): the true count is provably one of finitely many literal values, so a chain of `ite`s over literal divisors replaces the one nonlinear div, each linear individually. Java's truncating-toward-zero division direction (vs. SMT-LIB div's Euclidean convention) is preserved via the sign-correction ite already present. A String let-bound variable compares correctly against ANOTHER String-valued expression via the generic argResult/useEquality path (LetTranslationTest, real Z3, a genuine SAT/UNSAT-discriminating pair), but NOT against a bare string literal -- resolve(ExpConstString,...) only special-cases a literal against a direct ExpAttrOp receiver, not a let-bound ExpVariable, so `let s = a.name in s = 'literal'` still fails closed for that one narrower shape. All shapes outside these -- enum/U-type lets, non-`any`-initialized or non-strict-body object lets, `div` with any other divisor shape, a let-bound variable compared directly against a string literal -- remain located, fail-closed refusals.

unc-modelvalidator.evidence: Association navigation is supported in exactly two hard-coded shapes, both inside comparison(): (1) equality/inequality between two single-valued navigations of the same association (navigationEquals(), lines 101-113, reached via comparison()'s `l instanceof ExpNavigation ln && r instanceof ExpNavigation rn && !ln.getDestination().isCollection() && !rn.getDestination().isCollection()` guard at lines 87-90); (2) a collection-valued navigation used as the immediate range of exists() (visitExists(), lines 231-260, guarded at lines 235-238 to require ExpNavigation whose destination isCollection()). The GENERAL navigation entry point, visitNavigation() (lines 308-311), is reached for any OTHER use and unconditionally `throw unsupported("navigation")`. N-ary associations are separately hard-rejected earlier, at the model-loading layer: SmtModelFinder.java:188-194 requires ends.size()==2 for every configured association or throws IllegalArgumentException.
unc-modelvalidator.notes: Genuinely exercised and correct within its narrow scope: Library's noDoubleBorrowings (u.copy->exists(c1,c2|c1<>c2 and c1.book=c2.book)) exercises BOTH supported shapes at once -- u.copy as an exists() range (collection-valued navigation) and c1.book=c2.book as a navigation-equality comparison (single-valued navigation) -- and reaches SATISFIABLE on SMT-Z3. A third narrow shape was added for the attribute-access-through-navigation task: visitAttrOp() (lines 88-113) recognizes a receiver that is exactly one single-valued navigation hop away from a bare variable and routes it through navigatedAttribute() (lines 134-159) rather than through visitNavigation()'s unconditional refusal -- covering `<var>.<role>.<attr>` (e.g. Sudoku's self.row.index), reusing linkTerm() the same way navigationEquals() does. Every plain association therefore needs explicit _min/_max even when a Set{} literal is also given.

unc-modelvalidator.evidence: unc now derives association bounds from an explicit Set{} tuple literal and reproduces kk's setSpecificValues()+setLimits() arithmetic verbatim (ConfigurationReader.associationScope()), so the defect's INPUT condition does occur here -- but the contradictory result is REFUSED with its own message instead of being handed to a solver: 'association X predefines k forced link(s) but its derived bounds are min=k, max=...'. Confirmed by running kk's own AssociationConfigurator directly: k=134 with the defaulted (1,1) read yields min=134, max=1, and k=2/k=3 do the same.
unc-modelvalidator.notes: Kodkod only clears the contradiction through fixed-bitwidth wraparound, which this run measured rather than assumed: kk's own GraphColoring witness carries Adjacent#count=420 -- neither the 134 tuples the file pins nor the <=1 the derived maximum asks for. At bitwidth 8 both 420 and 134 wrap negative (-92 and -122), satisfying '>=134' and '<=1' simultaneously; at bitwidth 4/5/6 they wrap to 6, and the run is reported UNSATISFIABLE. That is a complete explanation of the bitwidth table documented in GraphColoring.properties' own header, which its author had left root-caused only as far as 'something needs bitwidth >= 8'. On unbounded SMT integers there is no such accident, so reproducing the literal bounds would emit a confident UNSAT; refusing is the honest outcome. 2026-08-29: went further -- diffed the real 420-tuple witness against the 134-tuple literal directly (not just the count). All 134 original tuples ARE present (setSpecificValues()'s forcing works correctly); 286 EXTRA, unintended tuples are also present (e.g. Region_r0's witness neighbors include r1/r3/r10/r14/r15/r17/r19/r20, none in the properties file's actual 4-neighbor edge list for r0) -- Kodkod is genuinely searching a materially different, ~3x denser graph-coloring problem, not the one specified. BUT checked whether this produces an observably WRONG verdict, and it does not, on either GraphColoring scenario: properColoring (r.neighbor->forAll(n|n.color<>r.color)) is monotonic non-decreasing under edge addition (a proper coloring of a supergraph is trivially still proper on any edge-subset; chromatic number never decreases when edges are added), so [main]'s SAT witness (all 134 true edges present, 286 extra) remains valid for the true 67-edge graph, and [twocolors]'s UNSAT (re-confirmed directly, ~429ms) stays correctly UNSAT since the true graph's odd 7-cycle already forces chromatic number >=3 regardless of what else is added. Both scenarios are immune to this real, confirmed bug purely by luck of this specific invariant's monotonicity, not because the mechanism is sound -- a non-monotonic invariant (e.g. an exact degree/size check) would not have this accidental protection. NOT (yet) promoted to a Study B supersession row: that would need a new, purpose-built minimal model with a non-monotonic association-bound-dependent invariant, the same way the four existing rows were each authored to demonstrate one clean mechanism -- flagged as a well-scoped follow-up, not attempted here.
unc-modelvalidator.coverageNote: GraphColoring and GraphColoring-UNSAT are the two rows that hit this; both ERROR with the dedicated refusal rather than reaching a verdict, so neither is cited. Adding 'Adjacent_min = 134 / Adjacent_max = 134' to that fixture would make the configuration internally consistent, but changing a shared corpus fixture is out of scope here.

features.name: Too-small bitwidth causes a false UNSATISFIABLE for internal/derived arithmetic not covered by the value-range warning

The 3-colorability claim itself is no longer just asserted from the construction method: examples/GraphColoring/valid-instance.soil hand-encodes an independently-computed (plain Python backtracking, not Kodkod) proper 3-coloring of this exact graph, and check -v confirms it satisfies properColoring -- so the false-negative really is the solver being wrong at low bitwidth, not the graph being miscategorized as 3-colorable.

unc-modelvalidator.evidence: This defect requires a bounded-bitvector integer encoding (Kodkod's two's-complement, fixed-width representation) to exist in the first place. SmtModelFinder.solve() hardcodes 'new SmtScript("QF_LIA")' (finder/SmtModelFinder.java:125) -- genuinely unbounded SMT-LIB Ints -- so there is no bitwidth-driven overflow mechanism for this specific false-negative failure mode to arise from.

Worked around in the example by using 'Field[*]' plus explicit .properties bounds instead. 2026-08-29: the SEVERITY was mischaracterized -- reproduced directly (both a minimal hand-built model and the real, unmodified original 9x9 use-core/.../Sudoku.use bundled example) and found the exception is NEVER visible to a caller of PluginModelFactory.getModel()/ModelTransformator.transform(): ModelTransformator.transform() (ModelTransformator.java:64-104) wraps its ENTIRE association+invariant transform pipeline in one try/catch(Exception), logs via LOG.error (log4j, invisible without a configured appender -- explaining every 'log4j:WARN No appenders could be found' line seen throughout this project's own probes) and returns the PARTIALLY-BUILT model regardless, with no re-throw and no error flag the caller can observe. Confirmed by direct inspection of the returned IModel for the real 9x9 Sudoku: transformClasses runs before the crash point, so all 5 classes survive; transformSimpleAssociations crashes partway through file-declaration-order iteration, so only the 3 associations declared BEFORE BoardFields (BoardRows/BoardColumns/BoardSquares) survive and BoardFields/RowFields/ColumnFields/SquareFields silently vanish; invariantTransformator.transformAndAdd() (line 93) is AFTER the crash point in the SAME try block, so it never runs at all -- the returned model has ZERO class invariants, not merely a missing association. IntegerConfigurator.atoms() (IntegerConfigurator.java:42-46) materialises the range as Integer atoms; RealConfigurator.atoms() (RealConfigurator.java:59-63) walks it by Real_step; StringConfigurator (StringConfigurator.java:24-28, 38-44, 57-60, 77-87) instead treats the range's UPPER bound as a COUNT of string atoms and pads the universe with generated 'String_string<i>' spellings, never reading String_min at all. AttributeConfigurator.upperBound() (AttributeConfigurator.java:117-182) is where it becomes an attribute's domain: with no per-attribute domainValues it takes the type's own upper bound (for Integer, filtered to the configured range plus the type's specific values, lines 129-164); with domainValues present it uses those ALONE (lines 168-181) and never consults the type range.
kk-modelvalidator.notes: Confirmed live on scenarios whose .properties really does leave an Integer attribute with no per-attribute key, so the fallback is the only thing bounding it: EmployeeInvariants (Employee.salary, only Integer_min/Integer_max = 0/3 in the section) reaches SATISFIABLE and EmployeeInvariants-UNSAT (Integer_min/Integer_max = -3/0) reaches UNSATISFIABLE under DefaultSAT4J; ZebraPuzzle (House.position, Integer_min/max = 0/6) reaches SATISFIABLE and ZebraPuzzle-UNSAT UNSATISFIABLE; GraphColoring (Region.color) and Sudoku (Row.index, Column.index, Square.index, Field.value) likewise, in both their SAT and UNSAT sections. The paired EmployeeInvariants sections are the sharpest evidence that the range is a real constraint and not just a registration: the two sections differ ONLY in Integer_min/Integer_max and flip the verdict.

unc-modelvalidator.evidence: The Integer and Real halves ARE supported: ConfigurationReader.addPrimitiveDomain() (config/ConfigurationReader.java:248-280) reads '<Type>_min'/'<Type>_max' into an AttributeDomain with an EMPTY className, using a separate typeWideDecimal() reader (ConfigurationReader.java:358-373) so that -1 stays an ordinary bound here while remaining the 'unset' sentinel for the per-attribute keys, and completing a one-sided range from the incumbent's own DEFAULT_TYPE_WIDE_MIN/MAX (ConfigurationReader.java:29-51). SmtModelFinder.registerTypeWideFallbackAttributes() (finder/SmtModelFinder.java:873-962) then encodes exactly those attributes of each scoped class that no per-attribute domain already registered, via AttributeEncoder.encode()'s ordinary range guard (encode/AttributeEncoder.java:421-427). Precedence matches the incumbent's AttributeConfigurator.upperBound:117/:168 branch: an explicit per-attribute domain wins outright and is never intersected with the type-wide range. The String half is NOT supported: String_min/String_max are refused as configuration diagnostics (ConfigurationReader.java:204-212) because the incumbent reads them as a COUNT of string atoms padded with generated placeholder spellings, which this encoding has no counterpart for; an unconfigured String attribute therefore still gets no symbol and its invariants are refused with ENCODING_SCOPE. Enum-typed attributes are likewise excluded (fallbackTypeOf(), SmtModelFinder.java:964-978) since no type-wide key exists for them and attributeTypeOf() cannot encode an enum at all.
unc-modelvalidator.notes: 2026-08-29: the 'blocked solely by a genuine OCL gap' claim is now STALE -- re-checked directly against the live benchmark run rather than trusted from this note's own prior wording. features.name: FRAGILE(j) macro: nominal target true AND U-aware target false AND others U-aware true

kk-modelvalidator.evidence: Structurally impossible for kk, not merely unimplemented: FRAGILE is defined as a DISCREPANCY BETWEEN TWO TRANSLATION MODES of the same invariant, and kk-modelvalidator has exactly one mode (see query.translation-modes) and no uncertainty representation to erase. kk-modelvalidator has no `query` configuration key: PropertyConfigurationVisitor (kk-modelvalidator/src/main/java/org/tzi/kodkod/model/config/impl/PropertyConfigurationVisitor.java) reads only class/association/attribute/invariant keys and reports containErrors()==false for a file carrying `query`, so the key is silently DROPPED rather than refused. Directly verifiable by running the corpus: the six ScenarioProfiles-* rows spell `query = exists satisfy`, `cover satisfy` and `uniform satisfy` over the same model and Kodkod returns the SAME outcome, TRIVIALLY_SATISFIABLE, for all six under DefaultSAT4J/LightSAT4J/Lingeling/MiniSat/MiniSatProver alike. unc-modelvalidator.evidence: SmtModelFinder.run (msc-modelvalidators/unc-modelvalidator/src/main/java/org/tzi/use/smt/finder/SmtModelFinder.java:202-250) dispatches on the profile: EXISTS is one solve with the scenario decoded back out of the assignment (:206-224); COVER solves one obligation per configured scenario, each free to pick its own snapshot; UNIFORM (:227-250) is ONE solve carrying every scenario at once with object/link/representative symbols declared once and SHARED, each scenario getting its own pinned uncertainty symbols and its own def/val pair.
